text:
Assertion (A) : The points A (1, 2), B (3, 4) and C (5, 6) are collinear.
Reason (R) : Three points A, B and C are collinear if AB + BC = AC.
option_a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
option_b: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
option_c: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
option_d: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
solution: AB = 2√2, BC = 2√2, AC = 4√2, so AB + BC = AC. Both are true and R explains A.

text:
Assertion (A) : The polynomial p(x) = x² + 3x + 3 has two real zeroes.
Reason (R) : The quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c, a ≠ 0, has two distinct real zeroes if b² – 4ac > 0.
option_a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
option_b: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
option_c: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
option_d: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
solution: For p(x), b² − 4ac = 9 − 12 = – 3 < 0, so it has no real zeroes: A is false. R is a true statement.

or_text: Two runners start running together around a circular track from the same point. One completes a round in 18 minutes and the other in 12 minutes. After how many minutes will they meet again at the starting point? How many rounds will the faster runner have completed by then?

or_solution: 18 = 2 × 3², 12 = 2² × 3, LCM = 2² × 3² = 36 minutes. The faster runner completes 3 rounds.

text: Given that √2 is an irrational number, prove that (5 – 3√2) is an irrational number.
scheme: Assume 5 − 3√2 = r, a rational number:1|Then √2 = (5 − r)/3, which is rational:1|Contradiction, so 5 − 3√2 is irrational:1
solution: If 5 − 3√2 = r (rational), then √2 = (5 − r)/3 would be rational, contradicting that √2 is irrational. Hence 5 − 3√2 is irrational.

topic: Tangents at the ends of a diameter
text: Prove that the tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are parallel.
scheme: Figure: diameter AB, tangents PQ at A and RS at B:1|OA ⟂ PQ and OB ⟂ RS (tangent ⟂ radius), so ∠OAQ = ∠OBR = 90°:1|These are alternate angles with transversal AB, so PQ ∥ RS:1
solution: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so ∠PAB = ∠ABS = 90°. These are equal alternate angles made by the transversal AB, hence the tangents are parallel.

text: Find the ratio in which the point P (– 4, 6) divides the line segment joining the points A (– 6, 10) and B (3, – 8). Also verify your answer using the y-coordinate of P.
scheme: Let the ratio be k : 1; x = (3k − 6)/(k + 1) = – 4:1|7k = 2, so the ratio is 2 : 7:1|Verify: y = (2(– 8) + 7(10))/9 = 6:1
solution: (3k − 6)/(k + 1) = – 4 gives k = 2/7, a ratio of 2 : 7. y = (– 16 + 70)/9 = 6, which matches.

text: Prove that: (1 + cot A – cosec A) (1 + tan A + sec A) = 2.
scheme: Write in sin and cos: (sin A + cos A − 1)/(sin A) × (cos A + sin A + 1)/(cos A):1|= ((sin A + cos A)² − 1)/(sin A cos A):1|= (2 sin A cos A)/(sin A cos A) = 2:1
solution: LHS = ((sin A + cos A − 1)(sin A + cos A + 1))/(sin A cos A) = (1 + 2 sin A cos A − 1)/(sin A cos A) = 2.
or_text: If sec θ + tan θ = p, then prove that sin θ = (p² − 1)/(p² + 1).
or_scheme: p² = ((1 + sin θ)²)/(cos² θ) = (1 + sin θ)/(1 − sin θ):1|Apply componendo-dividendo, or substitute into (p² − 1)/(p² + 1):1|Simplify to sin θ:1
or_solution: p² = ((1 + sin θ)²)/(1 − sin² θ) = (1 + sin θ)/(1 − sin θ). Then (p² − 1)/(p² + 1) = (2 sin θ)/2 = sin θ.

text:

On Tuesday, the price of each item was increased by ₹ 5 and the canteen sold 50 sandwiches and 20 glasses of juice, collecting ₹ 2,850. Let the price of a sandwich and a glass of juice on Monday be ₹ x and ₹ y respectively.
(i) Form a linear equation in two variables representing the sale on Monday. [1]
(ii) Form a linear equation in two variables representing the sale on Tuesday. [1]
(iii) (A) Find the price of a sandwich and a glass of juice on Monday. [2]
or_text:

topic: Case study: tangents to a flower bed
text:
In a school garden, a circular flower bed with centre O has a radius of 5 m. Riya stands at a point P outside the flower bed, 13 m away from the centre O, and two straight paths PA and PB from P touch the flower bed at the points A and B.
(i) What is the measure of ∠OAP? [1]
(ii) Find the length of the path PA. [1]
(iii) (A) Find the area of the quadrilateral OAPB. [2]
scheme: (i) ∠OAP = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius):1|(ii) PA = √(13² − 5²) = 12 m:1|(iii) (A) ar(OAPB) = 2 × ar(ΔOAP):1|(iii) (A) = 2 × 1/2 × 5 × 12 = 60 m²:1
or_text:
In a school garden, a circular flower bed with centre O has a radius of 5 m. Riya stands at a point P outside the flower bed, 13 m away from the centre O, and two straight paths PA and PB from P touch the flower bed at the points A and B.

(ii) Find the length of the path PA. [1]
(iii) (B) If the paths PA and PB were inclined to each other at an angle of 60°, then what would be the length of each path? [2]
or_scheme: (i) ∠OAP = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius):1|(ii) PA = √(13² − 5²) = 12 m:1|(iii) (B) ∠APO = 30°:1|(iii) (B) PA = OA/(tan 30°) = 5√3 m:1

text:
A construction company recorded the daily wages of 50 workers at one of its sites. The data is given below:
Daily wages (in ₹) | 100 – 150 | 150 – 200 | 200 – 250 | 250 – 300 | 300 – 350

scheme: (i) Modal class 200 – 250:1|(ii) N/2 = 25; cumulative frequencies 6, 15, 30, so the median class is 200 – 250:1|(iii) (A) Σfᵢxᵢ = 750 + 1575 + 3375 + 3300 + 2600 = 11600:1|(iii) (A) Mean = 11600/50 = ₹ 232:1
